sources.title: An ancient icon reveals new mysteries: mummy DNA resurrects a cryptic species within the Nile crocodile
sources.locator: Abstract; phylogenetic results; analysis of Egyptian mummy haplotypes.
sources.scope: Phylogenetic study combining modern African crocodile samples, karyotypes and Egyptian mummy DNA; supports the cryptic-lineage and historical Nile findings, not current abundance or a complete range estimate.
sources.attribution: Hekkala E et al. (2011). An ancient icon reveals new mysteries: mummy DNA resurrects a cryptic species within the Nile crocodile. Molecular Ecology 20(20):4199–4215. DOI 10.1111/j.1365-294X.2011.05245.x. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The study supported a cryptic lineage corresponding to Crocodylus suchus within the Nile crocodile complex and found mummy haplotypes consistent with historical occurrence of both crocodile lineages along the Nile.
claims.scope: Phylogenetic and historical-specimen evidence; not a present-day abundance or complete range assessment.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
Historical Nile mummy evidence does not establish current distribution limits, abundance, or conservation status.
